## Background magnetic field stabilizes QCD string against breaking

M. N. Chernodub*

Laboratoire  de Mathématiques et Physique Théorique; Université   Francois-Rabelais  Tours, Fédération Denis Poisson CNRS, de Grandmont; 37200 France Parc Tours,

DMPA, University of Gent; Krijgslaan  281, S9, B-9000 Gent;   Belgium

(Dated: January 3, 2010)

The confinement of quarks in hadrons occurs due to formation of QCD string: At separation between the quarks the QCD string breaks into pieces due to light  quark-antiquark pair creation We argue that there exist a critical background magnetic field eB ~ 16m? \_ above which the breaking is impossible in the transverse  directions with respect to the axis of the magnetic field. Thus; at strong enough magnetic field a new, asymmetrically confining phase may form The effect which can potentially be tested at LHC/ALICE experiment leads to abundance of u-quark rich hadrons and to excess of radially excited mesons in the noncentral heavy-ion collisions compared to the central ones large string

Some effects were also found in numerical simulations of lattice QCD. There exists numerical evidence in favor of existence of both the chiral magnetic effect [7] and the enhancement of the chiral symmetry breaking [8]. There are various potentially observable QCD effects associated with the presence of the strong magnetic field background. One can mention CP-odd generation of an electric current of quarks the axis of the mag netic field "the chiral magnetic effect" [2] and enhancement of the chiral symmetry breaking "the magnetic catalysis" )   [3] The latter is related to the fact that the background magnetic field makes the chiral condensate Acting through the chiral condensate; the magnetic field also shifts and strengthens the chiral transition [5]. along

A strong enough magnetic field affects the dynamics of the gluons through the ining fluence on the quarks, because the quarks are coupled to the both gauge fields [12].
